name: Azithromycin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Azithromycin is eliminated mainly in bile; about 6% appears unchanged in urine. In the US label's kidney study, exposure was nearly unchanged at a GFR of 10–80 mL/min, and peak level and AUC rose 61% and 35% below 10. The label gives no kidney dose change.
kidney_function_basis: Label PK study uses GFR (mL/min); no dose bands. Shown in the CrCl band rows.

bands.recommendation: No dose change stated (label). Exposure barely changes at GFR 10–80 (AUC +4%).

monitoring: QT interval in patients at risk (QT prolongation, low potassium or magnesium, bradycardia, class IA or III antiarrhythmics); liver tests if symptoms; INR with warfarin (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: 6 months and older (otitis media, sinusitis); 2 years and older (pharyngitis) (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Acute otitis media: 30 mg/kg once, or 10 mg/kg daily for 3 days, or 10 mg/kg on day 1 then 5 mg/kg on days 2 to 5. Acute sinusitis: 10 mg/kg daily for 3 days (label).
